description: Semantic capability layer: maps abstract intents extracted from problem statements to required Fabric capabilities, and capabilities to concrete Fabric item types. Complements signal-categories.json (lexical layer) — this registry handles intent→capability→items, signal-categories handles word→velocity→task-flow. ⚠️ AGENTS: Do NOT read this file directly — use capability-mapper.py instead.

intents.summary: User wants data scientists / ML practitioners to access and explore organizational data
intents.llm_hint: User is describing a gap between data availability and analytical/ML use of that data. Triggers Python/ML runtime + curated historical store.

intents.summary: User wants natural-language or AI-assisted querying of data
intents.llm_hint: User wants non-technical users (analysts, executives) to interrogate data without writing SQL or KQL. Triggers DataAgent with governed semantic context.

intents.summary: User has long historical record and wants to derive value from it
intents.llm_hint: User has a large historical corpus that needs cheap durable storage AND a structure suitable for analytical workloads (medallion bronze/silver/gold).

intents.summary: User has manual/paper-based field intake and wants to digitize it
intents.llm_hint: User has humans in the field capturing data manually. Triggers a low-code mobile/form-friendly ingest path (Power Apps + CopyJob/DataPipeline into lakehouse bronze).

intents.summary: User needs sub-minute (often sub-second) reaction to incoming signals
intents.llm_hint: User cannot tolerate batch latency. Triggers Eventstream (ingest) + Eventhouse (low-latency store) + KQL Dashboard or Real-Time Dashboard (serve).

intents.summary: User wants automated alerts or actions when thresholds are crossed
intents.llm_hint: User needs reactive automation. Triggers Activator/Reflex on top of the streaming or analytical layer.

intents.summary: User explicitly prefers low-code or SQL-first tooling for ingestion/transforms
intents.llm_hint: User wants to keep existing SQL/BI team productive without forcing them into PySpark. Bias ingestion toward CopyJob/DataPipeline/Dataflow Gen2.

intents.summary: User wants code-first Python/Spark for ML/AI workloads even if other workloads are low-code
intents.llm_hint: User has or wants ML practitioners working in code. Triggers Notebook (Python/PySpark) bound to Lakehouse + optional MLModel/MLExperiment.

intents.summary: User wants governed semantic model for analyst self-service reporting
intents.llm_hint: User wants governed BI consumption. Triggers SemanticModel + Report layered on Lakehouse SQL endpoint or Warehouse.

intents.summary: User must handle regulated, sensitive, or governed data
intents.llm_hint: User has regulatory obligations. Triggers Variable Library for secrets + workspace-level governance + sensitivity labels.

capabilities.summary: A Python/PySpark execution environment bound to lakehouse storage, suitable for data-science exploration and ML training.
Durable, cheap, multi-zone (bronze/silver/gold) store for years of structured + semi-structured history with Spark + SQL access.
Natural-language interface over governed data — users ask plain-English questions, the platform answers from curated sources.
An ingest path optimized for mobile/field-form submissions (replacing pen-and-paper).
A low-latency event/time-series store sized for seconds-class KQL queries on streaming data.
Native streaming ingest from sensors, message brokers, or change-data-capture sources.
Automated trigger/alert mechanism that fires on threshold conditions in streaming or analytical data.
Low-code or no-code ingestion path for SQL-first teams: scheduled bulk + incremental loads without Spark.
Governed semantic layer + reporting surface for analyst self-service over the lakehouse or warehouse.
Centralized secrets and parameter management for environment-aware deployment.
